power.title: Power Analysis Check
report:
::: {.callout-tip title="Learn More" collapse="true"}

Power analyses need to contain the following information to be interpretable: the type of power analysis, the statistical test, the software used, sample size, critical alpha criterion, power level, effect size, and an effect size metric. In addition, it is recommended to make sure the power analysis is reproducible (by sharing the code, or a screenshot, of the power analysis), and to provide good arguments for why the study was designed to detect an effect of this size.

For an a-priori power analysis, where the sample size is determined, reporting all information would look like:

> An a priori power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that for a Cohen's d = 0.5, an alpha level of 0.05, and a desired power level of 80% required at least 64 participants in each group.

For a sensitivity power analysis, this sentence would look like:

> A sensitivity power analysis for an independent samples t-test, conducted using the pwr.t.test function from pwr (Champely, 2020), indicated that with 64 participants in each group, and an alpha level of 0.05, a desired power level of 80% was reached for an effect size of d = 0.5.

:::

text.text: Purpose Germline shelterin variants were linked to sarcoma in a case-enriched cohort.
Whether shelterin loss of function predisposes to mesenchymal neoplasia in the general population is unknown.
Methods We analyzed rare-variant collapsing associations for five shelterin genes across neoplasm phenotypes in UK Biobank exomes, with Genebass as a second pipeline.
Prespecified shelterin and centrosome gene sets were tested by permutation-calibrated statistics against a TP53/RB1/NF1 positive control.
Carrier risks were compared with telomere-lengthening predictions.

Lipoma risk was increased in TERF1 (odds ratio [OR], 3.32; P = 8.4 × 10 ), ⁻⁸ POT1, and TERF2IP carriers, and uterine leiomyoma risk in all four core shelterin genes, most strongly POT1 (OR, 2.23; P = 4.0 × 10 ); POT1 and TINF2 reproduced in Genebass.
⁻⁵ TERF1 was also associated with thyroid cancer and monoclonal gammopathy.
Neither gene set nor the positive control was associated with self-reported sarcoma.
Telomere lengthening accounted for POT1-associated chronic lymphocytic leukemia risk but not myeloma or TINF2-associated thyroid cancer, where observed risk exceeded prediction five-to seven-fold.
Conclusion Shelterin loss of function is a population-level risk factor for lipoma and uterine leiomyoma, the benign counterparts of liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma.
TERF1 joins POT1 and TINF2 as long-telomere cancer genes.
Sarcoma-specific penetrance remains untested.

Sarcomas have the highest heritable fraction of any adult solid tumor, yet most familial and early-onset cases remain unexplained after testing for TP53 and the classic predisposition syndromes. 1 Wholegenome sequencing of the International Sarcoma Kindred Study recently implicated rare variants in the shelterin complex (POT1, TINF2, TERF1, TERF2IP) and in centrosome genes (CEP63, CEP72, HAUS4, HAUS5). 2 These genes now appear on expanded sarcoma panels, but the association derives from a caseenriched cohort and has not been replicated.

text.text: Shelterin caps chromosome ends and restrains telomerase; its loss of function lengthens telomeres. [3] [4] [5] Telomere-lengthening POT1 and TINF2 variants cause familial melanoma, chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL), thyroid cancer, glioma, and cardiac angiosarcoma. [6] [7] [8] [9] [10] [11] [12] Population studies have since established three points: rare POT1, TERF1, and TINF2 truncating variants lengthen leukocyte telomere length (LTL) in UK Biobank; 13 POT1 carriers in UK Biobank have an eight-fold risk of lymphoid malignancy; 12 and genetically longer telomeres cause CLL, melanoma, thyroid cancer, and myeloma. 14 Uterine fibroids have been noted in POT1 long-telomere kindreds. 12 Three questions remain open.

text.text: First, whether the shelterin spectrum extends to mesenchymal neoplasia, which would give the sarcoma association a lineage-specific basis.
Second, whether TERF1 and TERF2IP, which lengthen telomeres but lack established cancer phenotypes, share the spectrum.
Third, whether telomere length alone accounts for carrier risk.
We addressed these questions, and tested the proposed sarcoma genes directly, using population exome and genome-wide association resources.
This study used publicly available summary statistics.

Gene-level rare-variant associations came from UK Biobank whole-exome sequencing, analyzed through the AstraZeneca PheWAS portal 15 and, as a second analytic pipeline, Genebass. 16 Outcome genome-wide association statistics came from FinnGen release 12. 17 Institutional review was not required for deidentified summary data.
text.formatted: Gene-level rare-variant associations came from UK Biobank whole-exome sequencing, analyzed through the AstraZeneca PheWAS portal <ref type="bibr" target="#b14">15</ref> and, as a second analytic pipeline, Genebass. <ref type="bibr" target="#b15">16</ref> Outcome genome-wide association statistics came from FinnGen release 12. <ref type="bibr" target="#b16">17</ref> Institutional review was not required for deidentified summary data.

text.text: The two resources analyze substantially the same individuals: 459,449 participants of European ancestry in the AstraZeneca release used here and 394,841 in Genebass, drawn from the same UK Biobank exome tranche, so the Genebass sample is largely contained within the AstraZeneca sample.
Agreement between them therefore tests variant masks, quality control, and test statistics rather than sampling.

We extracted results for POT1, TERF1, TERF2, TERF2IP, and TINF2 across all neoplasm-related binary phenotypes (ICD-10 cancer registry, hospital inpatient, death registry, self-report, histology, and union definitions) and LTL in individuals of European ancestry.
The portal export retained gene-modelphenotype results at P ≤ .10 (1,118 phenotypes).
Four collapsing models were considered: proteintruncating variants (PTV); PTV plus rare damaging missense (PTV + RDM); ultra-rare variants; and synonymous variants as a negative control.
Binary associations are ORs with 95% CIs (Fisher's exact test).

The prespecified mesenchymal outcomes were benign lipomatous neoplasm (ICD-10 D17), uterine leiomyoma (D25), soft-tissue malignancy (C49), mesothelial and soft-tissue malignancy (C45-C49), bone malignancy (C40-C41), and connective tissue histology (ICD-O-3 8800-9370).
Union definitions (any source) were primary.
We treat P < 1 × 10 as robust in this five-gene analysis, ⁻⁵ P < .05 as nominal, and concordance across genes as supporting evidence.

text.text: For uterine leiomyoma (D25; 9,560 cases) and 37 ICD-10 cancer sites, we retrieved Genebass pLoF and synonymous burden and SKAT-O 18 results for the six shelterin genes (adding ACD).

From Genebass, we retrieved exome-wide gene-level results for self-reported sarcoma or fibrosarcoma (208 cases), thyroid cancer (C73; 340 cases), and melanoma (C43; 2,024 cases) for pLoF, pLoF plus missense, and synonymous masks.

Seven sets were prespecified: shelterin core (POT1, TERF1, TINF2, TERF2IP), all six shelterin genes, an extended telomere set (adding SMARCAL1, TIMELESS, STAG3, CTC1, NHP2), centrosome core (CEP63, CEP72, HAUS4, HAUS5), an extended centrosome set (adding CEP89, SSNA1, PCM1, CEP57, MZT1), the combined core, and a positive control (TP53, RB1, NF1), mirroring the discovery study. 2 Sets were tested with a directional Stouffer statistic of signed burden z scores and a nondirectional aggregated Cauchy association test (ACAT) 19 of SKAT-O P values.

text.text: We estimated the causal effect of LTL on CLL, thyroid cancer, melanoma, and multiple myeloma by twosample Mendelian randomization (MR), using 101 LTL instruments (mean F, 134) 20 and FinnGen R12 outcomes.

text.text: The primary estimator was inverse-variance weighted (IVW) MR, 21 with MR-Egger, 22 weighted median, 23 and exclusion of telomere-biology loci as sensitivity analyses.

text.text: For each lead genecancer pair, we computed the risk predicted by telomere lengthening alone as exp( LTL × IVW), Δ β where LTL is the carrier LTL difference in SD units and IVW the log OR per SD, with 95% CIs from Δ β the MR standard error.
Observed-to-predicted ratios above 1 indicate risk not explained by telomere length under a log-linear model.
Analyses used Python 3 with pandas, NumPy, SciPy, and matplotlib; the permutation seed was 2026.
P values are two-sided except the directional gene-set statistic, which is one-sided for risk; ACAT is nondirectional.
All analyses are complete-case on published summary statistics.
The prespecified mesenchymal family comprised six phenotypes, five genes, and four collapsing models (120 tests; Bonferroni = 4.2 × 10 ⁴).
Because the models are nested and union phenotypes contain α ⁻ their source-specific components, these tests are correlated and Bonferroni is conservative.

We therefore prespecified P < 1 × 10 as robust, ⁻⁵ P < 4.2 × 10 ⁴ as family-wise significant, and ⁻ P < .05 as nominal, and required concordance across genes or across pipelines before interpreting a nominal result.

Synonymous collapsing models were a within-gene negative control, and TP53, RB1, and NF1 a betweengene positive control for sarcoma.

The AstraZeneca PheWAS and Genebass analyses draw on overlapping UK Biobank participants, so their agreement tests analytic robustness across different variant masks, quality control, and test statistics rather than replication in an independent sample.
For each phenotype and mask, gene-level burden estimates were converted to signed z scores, z = sign( ) × ¹(1β Φ⁻ P/2), and combined as Σz/√k.
The null distribution was 100,000 random sets of k genes drawn without replacement from the 17,522 to 19,020 genes with non-missing burden results in that stratum, with empirical P = (b + 1)/(B + 1).
Random sets were matched on gene count only, not on cumulative allele frequency or variant count.
ACAT combined SKAT-O P values over 20,000 random sets.

Genebass returns a SKAT-O P of exactly 1 for genes with too few qualifying variants (64.7% of genes for sarcoma, 52.0% for thyroid cancer, and 18.1% for melanoma), and one such gene saturates the Cauchy statistic; gene sets containing one are reported as not evaluable.
The null is affected in the same way: 95% to 99.8% of random sets for thyroid cancer contain a saturated gene and sit at the ceiling, so an evaluable observed set appears extreme against them.
ACAT was therefore calibrated against random sets drawn from evaluable genes only.
Calibration against the whole gene pool, the conventional choice, returns P values two-to 549-fold smaller here and is anticonservative.

text.text: In roughly 450,000 exomes, shelterin loss of function predisposed to lipoma and uterine leiomyoma, the benign counterparts of liposarcoma and leiomyosarcoma.

The association was shared by all four core shelterin genes, reproduced for leiomyoma in a second analytic pipeline, and absent for synonymous variants and for the shelterin genes with minimal telomere effects.
TERF1, the gene with the largest telomere effect, also conferred risk of thyroid cancer, MGUS, and lymphoid malignancy, placing it beside POT1 and TINF2 as long-telomere cancer genes.
The sarcoma and centrosome associations reported from a case-enriched cohort could not be tested adequately, because the sarcoma outcome lacked power even for positive-control genes.

These findings give the reported shelterin-sarcoma association a lineage-specific basis. 2 Leiomyosarcoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma are the most common adult soft-tissue sarcomas, and both depend on telomere maintenance through TERT activation or ATRX/DAXX-associated alternative lengthening of telomeres.
text.formatted: These findings give the reported shelterin-sarcoma association a lineage-specific basis. <ref type="bibr" target="#b1">2</ref> Leiomyosarcoma and dedifferentiated liposarcoma are the most common adult soft-tissue sarcomas, and both depend on telomere maintenance through TERT activation or ATRX/DAXX-associated alternative lengthening of telomeres.

text.text: A germline state that expands smooth muscle and adipocytic precursor pools, as the leiomyoma and lipoma associations imply, would enlarge the substrate for malignant transformation in precisely these lineages.
The direction and magnitude of the malignant soft-tissue estimates (ORs, 3 to 5 for POT1 and TERF1) are consistent with this model, although each rests on four or five carriers.

The model predicts that shelterin carriers with sarcoma will be enriched for leiomyosarcoma and liposarcoma histology, and that their tumors will less often require somatic TERT or ALT activation; both predictions are testable in sequenced sarcoma cohorts.
The mesenchymal associations extend a recognized clinical observation.

Uterine fibroids were noted in POT1 long-telomere kindreds, 12 and our data show that this is a population-level phenotype shared by all four core shelterin genes, with an approximately two-fold risk in carriers of each; TERF2 and ACD, which barely alter telomere length, were null.
text.formatted: Uterine fibroids were noted in POT1 long-telomere kindreds, <ref type="bibr" target="#b11">12</ref> and our data show that this is a population-level phenotype shared by all four core shelterin genes, with an approximately two-fold risk in carriers of each; TERF2 and ACD, which barely alter telomere length, were null.

text.text: Lipoma has not, to our knowledge, been linked to germline telomere biology.

The strength of the TERF1-lipoma association (P = 8.4 × 10 ), its presence in ⁻⁸ hospital-coded records, and its concentration in truncal and intra-abdominal sites argue against ascertainment artifact.
Intra-abdominal lipomatous tumors deserve attention because welldifferentiated liposarcoma can be coded as lipoma at that site.
Our leiomyoma results have to be read against a prior exome-wide search of the same resource.

Välimäki et al. tested approximately 19,000 genes against the identical AstraZeneca portal endpoint under ten collapsing models and reported eight genes meeting odds ratio > 2.0 with P < 1 × 10 ⁴, all ⁻ converging on the SRCAP chromatin-remodeling complex; no shelterin gene was among them. 24 The difference is case accrual, not effect size.

text.text: Their release held 15,780 cases of this endpoint against the 19,193 analyzed here.

Rescaling our POT1 carrier counts to their case and control totals leaves the odds ratio unchanged (2.22 v 2.23) but moves P to 1.1 × 10 ⁴ for PTV + RDM and 3.8 × 10 ⁴ for PTV, both ⁻ ⁻ outside their reporting threshold.
Shelterin and SRCAP are therefore best read as independent moderate-penetrance routes to uterine leiomyoma, the shelterin route distinguished by its extension to extrauterine adipocytic neoplasia.
Telomere length did not account for all carrier risk.

The POT1-CLL association matched the risk predicted from telomere lengthening, consistent with prolonged B-cell replicative capacity driving clonal expansion. 5, 12, 25 But POT1-associated myeloma and TINF2-associated thyroid cancer 26 exceeded predictions five-to seven-fold, and mesenchymal tumor risk was similar for TERF2IP and POT1 despite a six-fold difference in telomere elongation.

text.text: Shelterin proteins have functions beyond length control, including suppression of ATR and ATM signaling at telomeres and protection against telomere fusion. 3 Partial loss of these functions may create chromosomal instability that adds to the proliferative advantage of long telomeres.

text.text: Alternatively, leukocyte telomere length may understate elongation in target tissues.
Either way, telomere length measurement alone will underestimate the risk carried by these variants.
The centrosome findings argue for caution.
Neither core nor extended centrosome sets showed a directional pLoF signal for any outcome.

Centrosome variants may confer risk specific to sarcoma or to early-onset disease, which an adult cohort recruited at ages 40 to 69 years cannot capture; until replicated, these genes should not be interpreted clinically.
There are clinical implications.
Shelterin variants identified on sarcoma panels should prompt counseling on the established long-telomere spectrum (CLL and myeloma, thyroid cancer, melanoma), 27 which should now include TERF1.
text.formatted: Shelterin variants identified on sarcoma panels should prompt counseling on the established long-telomere spectrum (CLL and myeloma, thyroid cancer, melanoma), <ref type="bibr" target="#b26">27</ref> which should now include TERF1.

text.text: The mesenchymal findings do not justify surveillance for lipoma or leiomyoma, which are common and benign, but they support considering shelterin genes as candidate predisposition genes in patients with leiomyosarcoma or liposarcoma, particularly with a personal or family history of the long-telomere spectrum.
This study has limitations.
The AstraZeneca and Genebass analyses draw on overlapping UK Biobank participants; the second pipeline controls for analytic choices, not sampling, and independent replication is required.
The portal export omitted results with P > .10, precluding a complete forest of null associations and formal heterogeneity testing across genes.
text.formatted: The portal export omitted results with P > .10, precluding a complete forest of null associations and formal heterogeneity testing across genes.

text.text: Lipoma and leiomyoma were ascertained from hospital and self-report records and are underdiagnosed, which should bias toward the null.

Several associations rest on fewer than ten carriers, particularly the TERF1 associations with MGUS, choroidal melanoma, and intra-abdominal lipoma, and nominal P values across many phenotypes carry a false-positive expectation, which we mitigated by prespecifying mesenchymal outcomes and requiring cross-gene concordance.
Analyses were restricted to European ancestry.
The observed-versus-predicted comparison assumes a log-linear MR effect that may not hold at the extreme elongation seen in carriers.
Sarcoma ascertainment was inadequate for direct inference, as the null positive control shows.

In conclusion, germline shelterin loss of function predisposes to benign adipocytic and smooth muscle neoplasia at population scale, providing a lineage-specific rationale for its reported association with sarcoma.
TERF1 is a long-telomere cancer gene, and carrier risk exceeds what telomere length alone predicts for several cancers.
Resolving sarcoma-specific penetrance will require sarcoma-enriched sequencing with histology-level phenotypes and tumor telomere maintenance status.
